name: Hexanies (Combination Product Sets)
characteristics: 6-note scales. Very pure harmony, but chord progressions only weakly imply a tonal center. 'Dreamy and flighty' sound. Lower numbers (1-3-5-7) sound more familiar; higher numbers (11/13) sound more alien.
history: Studied extensively by Erv Wilson. Part of the Eikosany family structure.
performance_tips: Mapped to keys C, D, E, G, A, B. Middle C (MIDI 60) is tuned to F# (369.99Hz). Use for static, pure harmonic textures.

name: Dekanies (Combination Product Sets)
characteristics: 10-note scales. Similar pure harmony to Hexanies but with more melodic possibilities. The inclusion of the 11th and 13th harmonics creates unique 'xenharmonic' timbres.
history: Developed from Erv Wilson's CPS theories.
performance_tips: Mapped to keys C, D, D#, E, F, F#, G, A, A#, B. Middle C is tuned to F#.

name: Eikosany 1-3-5-7-9-11
characteristics: 20-note scale. A massive structure containing pure intervals including the undecimal comma (1/4 tone), Ptolemy's second, and harmonic sevenths. Offers vast harmonic territories.
history: An advanced CPS structure studied by Erv Wilson and Kraig Grady.
performance_tips: Laid out linearly; every 20 keys span an octave. Can be 'unwieldy' to play; suggested for advanced exploration of Just Intonation relationships.

name: ED3 Family (Equal Divisions of 3/1)
characteristics: These scales do not repeat at the octave (2/1) but at the perfect twelfth (3/1). 19-ED3 is a stretched version of 12-TET; 8-ED3 is a stretched 5-TET.
history: Conceptually related to the Bohlen-Pierce scale (13-ED3).
performance_tips: Since there are no octaves, chord inversions are impossible. Harmonies appear in unexpected places. Rely on ear rather than theory.

name: EDphi Family (Equal Divisions of Phi)
characteristics: Divides the Golden Ratio (Phi) into equal parts. Phi is acoustically the most dissonant interval. Creates an 'ocean of chaos' without stable octaves.
history: Experimental tunings based on mathematical constants found in nature.
performance_tips: Expect high dissonance. Useful for chaotic, inharmonic, or textural soundscapes where conventional resolution is not desired.

name: CET Scales
characteristics: Scales that repeat at specific small intervals measured in cents, creating cyclical structures that do not align with the octave.
history: Modern experimental tuning concepts.
performance_tips: Similar to other non-octave scales: melodic contours will not repeat clearly across registers.

name: Meantone (and 19-TET)
characteristics: Includes historical well-temperaments and 19-TET. 19-TET offers a familiar diatonic feel but with more consonance in thirds and distinct sharps/flats.
history: The dominant tuning system of Western music for hundreds of years before 12-TET. 19-TET is a natural extension.
performance_tips: Good for extending common practice harmony. In 19-TET, C# and Db are distinct notes.

name: Mavila
characteristics: Described as 'Meantone's anti-matter'. Inverts the major scale structure (TTSTTTs becomes ssTsssT). Major chords become minor, minor become major.
history: A regular temperament that flips harmonic expectations.
performance_tips: Try playing songs you know; they will sound 'inside-out' (happy songs become sad/minor).

name: Blackwood
characteristics: Formed by 2 interlocking chains of 5-TET. Allows major or minor triads from any root. No diminished chords exist in this scale.
history: Named after Easley Blackwood.
performance_tips: Allows for continuous modulation upwards without hitting dissonant 'wolf' intervals found in standard tuning.

name: Superpyth
characteristics: Fifths are sharper than standard. Major thirds become very sharp (bright/jarring), minor thirds become very flat (gloomy).
history: An extension of Pythagorean tuning principles.
performance_tips: Use for high contrast between major (intense brightness) and minor (dark gloom).

name: Pajara
characteristics: 10-note scales based on 22-TET tonality. Uses notes found in blues melodies to extend harmony. Chords sound familiar but connect in new ways.
history: Based on a paper by Paul Erlich regarding 22-TET decatonic scales.
performance_tips: Great for 'bluesy' or xenharmonic harmonic progressions that still retain a melodic logic.

name: Machine
characteristics: 6-note scale resembling a stretched major or whole-tone scale. Features the 7th (Barbershop) and 11th (semi-augmented 4th) harmonics.
history: Modern regular temperament.
performance_tips: Produces chords resembling 'dominant 9 #11' without the 3rd or 5th. Great for mechanical or futuristic textures.

name: Orwell
characteristics: Features 7th and 11th harmonics plus 'subminor' thirds. Does not have recognizable major/minor thirds but offers pleasing melodic intervals.
history: Named in reference to the 1984 dystopian aesthetic or complexity.
performance_tips: Use for complex chords that are stable yet alien, lacking the standard major/minor emotional dichotomy.

name: Porcupine
characteristics: Contains familiar chords mixed in a different order, extended to include the 11th harmonic.
history: A popular temperament in the xenharmonic community.
performance_tips: Stacking three minor thirds results in a minor seventh (unlike the major sixth in 12-TET), allowing for 'musical puns' and unexpected resolutions.

name: Lemba
characteristics: Repeats at the tritone (half-octave) rather than the octave. Symmetrical scale with three types of thirds.
history: Rank-2 temperament with tritone equivalence.
performance_tips: Playing a full octave yields a symmetrical scale. Useful for symmetrical harmonic motion.

name: Indonesian Gamelan (Slendro & Pelog)
characteristics: Slendro: 5-note scale with roughly equidistant intervals (mapped to black keys). Pelog: 7-note scale with unequal intervals (mapped to white keys).
history: Averages of measured gamelans from Java (Surjodiningrat 1993, Kunst 1949).
performance_tips: Authenticity is difficult as every Gamelan is tuned uniquely. Use for metallophone textures.

name: Arabic Maqam
characteristics: Modal system involving quarter tones and neutral intervals. 'Rast' is a fundamental mode.
history: Traditional system of melodic modes used in Arabic music.
performance_tips: Maqam implies improvisation techniques, not just a scale. Pitch bending and ornamentation are essential.

name: Thai Ranat
characteristics: Roughly 7-TET (7 equal tones per octave), but this version is a specific measurement from a 'Ceremonial and Court Music' record.
history: Tuning of the Ranat (Thai xylophone).
performance_tips: Mapped to white keys. Great for rapid, percussive, equidistantly-spaced melodies.

name: Bagpipes (Scotland, Bulgaria, Macedonia)
characteristics: Scotland: Neutral intervals (between minor/major). Bulgaria: Pure major 3rd. Macedonia: Exotic intervals.
history: Measured from traditional instruments (Anaphoria archive).
performance_tips: Use drone notes. Scottish mapped to white keys; others have specific chromatic mappings.

name: North Indian Ragas
characteristics: Just Intonation based scales. Distinct ascending (Aroha) and descending (Avaroha) lines.
history: Ancient Indian classical tradition where tuning depends on the mood/time of day.
performance_tips: Note that real Raga performance involves specific emphasis and ornamentation, not just the raw pitches. 'Shrutis' file contains the full 22-note gamut.

name: Ancient Greek Genera
characteristics: Based on Tetrachords (4 strings). Categories: Diatonic (tones/semitone), Chromatic (minor 3rd + semitones), Enharmonic (Major 3rd + quartertones).
history: Recorded by Ptolemy and others (4th century BC - 2nd century AD).
performance_tips: Mapped to white keys, tonic on E. Intended for lyre-like plucking.

name: Zimbabwe Mbira
characteristics: Measured from a specific instrument made by Josephat Mandaza (2002).
history: Shona music tradition.
performance_tips: Instrument uses metal strips (lamellophone). The scale covers multiple octaves with specific mapping to white keys.

name: High-Accuracy Regular Temperaments
characteristics: 12-Adams: consonant but modulates sharply. zeus7tri: few perfect 4ths/5ths, 11th harmonic focus. elfmadagascar9: subminor 3rds. glummamarvwoo: tempered Glumma scale.
history: Included based on feedback from microtonal musicians wanting accuracy over 'trippy' sounds.
performance_tips: These are less about 'effect' and more about specific structural properties for composition.
